title: Optimizing Distributed Artifact Generation with BuildKit
business: Large-scale software engineering organizations managing complex, multi-language microservices.
problem: Redundant compilation steps across distributed CI/CD pipelines lead to excessive build times and wasted compute resources when intermediate layers are not shared.
solution: BuildKit utilizes a binary intermediate format called LLB to define dependency graphs, enabling concurrent execution and efficient instruction caching that persists across distributed environments.
steps: Deploy the buildkitd daemon on dedicated build nodes to manage the solver and cache.
Configure the buildctl client to communicate with the daemon via gRPC or TCP.
Define build logic using a frontend like dockerfile.v0 or custom LLB-based definitions.
Enable cache export and import using the registry type to share intermediate layers between independent CI runners.
Execute builds using buildctl, specifying the remote cache source to leverage existing layers.
outcome: Reduced total build duration through parallelized dependency resolution and high cache hit rates across the CI/CD fleet.
limitation: Cache invalidation can be complex when using max mode; verify cache effectiveness by monitoring build logs for cache hit/miss indicators during execution.

diagram.title: BuildKit Distributed Caching Flow
diagram.description: The flow shows how buildctl interacts with the daemon and registry to optimize builds.

code.content:
# Build with remote cache import and export
buildctl build \
  --frontend=dockerfile.v0 \
  --local context=. \
  --output type=image,name=my-registry/app:latest,push=true \
  --export-cache type=registry,ref=my-registry/app:cache,mode=max \
  --import-cache type=registry,ref=my-registry/app:cache # Reuses layers from previous runs
code.explanation: This command demonstrates how to leverage the registry cache exporter to persist and reuse build layers, directly addressing the problem of redundant compilation.
